research_question: In people with cancer receiving radiotherapy (with or without concurrent chemotherapy), do probiotics compared with placebo reduce the incidence of grade 2 or higher (moderate-to-severe) diarrhoea?
outcome_description: Incidence (number of patients / proportion) of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea during or shortly after pelvic/abdominal radiotherapy, graded with RTOG, CTCAE, WHO or comparable toxicity criteria; also accepting reported moderate-to-severe radiation-induced diarrhoea when explicit grading thresholds are given.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR below 1 / positive Hedges g) means probiotics reduced the incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea relative to placebo.
search_queries: Lactobacillus radiotherapy diarrhea placebo controlled cancer
probiotic supplementation chemoradiotherapy gastrointestinal toxicity incidence
inclusion_criteria: Studies of patients with cancer receiving radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy, that administered probiotics (any strain, dose, or formulation) to at least one group
Includes a placebo or otherwise untreated/standard-care comparison group
Reports any quantitative data on diarrhoea or gastrointestinal toxicity, including event counts, proportions, severity grades, or summary statistics
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/protocol paper)
No comparison between a probiotic (treatment) condition and a placebo or control condition
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or odds/risk ratios reported)
Completely unrelated to probiotics and radiotherapy-associated gastrointestinal outcomes in cancer patients
moderators_to_extract: Probiotic formulation (single-strain vs multi-strain) and species
Probiotic dose (CFU/day) and duration of administration
Irradiated site (pelvic, abdominal, gynaecologic, colorectal, head and neck)
Diarrhoea grading system used (RTOG, CTCAE, WHO)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias / blinding status
effect_size_note: Primary pooling as risk ratio (RR) of grade ≥2 diarrhoea using event counts and group sizes, random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) with Mantel-Haenszel weighting; RR < 1 favours probiotics. Zero-event studies handled with a continuity correction where required.
single_outcome_target: Incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea
